what: Ecopetrol is Colombia's state-controlled oil company. It produces oil and gas in Colombia and the US Permian basin, refines fuel in Colombia, and owns most of the country's oil pipelines and a large electricity transmission business.
customers: Colombian fuel distributors, international crude buyers, and electricity users through its transmission subsidiary ISA.
moat: Control of Colombia's oil infrastructure, from the wells to the pipelines to the refineries, with no domestic competitor of comparable scale.
risks: The Colombian government controls it and has restricted new exploration licences
Debt of about $36 billion against $5 billion of cash
Revenue fell about 10% last year with oil prices
Colombian reserves are declining and replacement has been difficult
opportunities: The ISA transmission business provides regulated earnings unrelated to oil
Permian basin assets give production growth outside Colombia
watch: Reserve replacement, Colombian production volumes, and the government's dividend policy.
